what_this_is: A machine re-read of both shop pages behind each of the 44 two-shop price comparisons, compared with the price, pack and availability stored in the frozen 2026-11-16 vintage. It is not a human verification and it is not an independent parse for either shop.

MedPlus.catches: page changed after collection, product withdrawn, price moved
MedPlus.cannot_catch: a parser that has always read the field wrongly

HealthPlus.intended_result: 0 of 44 read: HTTP 429 'local_rate_limited' on every attempt, including two attempts 60 s apart and one batch stopped after two consecutive 429s
HealthPlus.why_not: scrapers/healthplus.py reads /products.json (line 97); the fallback is the scraper's own source
HealthPlus.catches: page changed after collection, product withdrawn, price moved, product no longer in the published catalogue
HealthPlus.cannot_catch: a scraper that has always mapped a field wrongly

structural_findings.finding: two comparison rows are two different products under one name
structural_findings.detail: 44 comparison rows sit on 42 distinct (name, state) pairs. 'Amlodipine / Lagos' and 'Vitamin B Complex / Lagos' each appear twice, from different product ids, so a reader sees the same drug name twice at very different prices.
structural_findings.source: scripts/dbq.py "select canonical_name, state, count(*) ... from v_cheapest_per_product_state where is_comparison group by 1,2 having count(*)>1"

structural_findings.finding: a 100 ml syrup is recorded with pack size 100, the same field as 100 tablets
structural_findings.detail: product_id 1037 is 'Emplex Vitamin B Complex Syrup 100ml'; its comparison row carries pack_size 100 with no unit in the row, so any per-unit arithmetic reads it as 100 doses. pharmacy_listings.pack_unit exists; v_cheapest_per_product_state does not expose it.

structural_findings.finding: no independent parse was obtained for either shop today
structural_findings.detail: MedPlus was read through data-product-price, the field the scraper reads. The HealthPlus /products/<handle>.js endpoint, which is the independent channel the script is built on, answered 429 'local_rate_limited' throughout; the fallback used was /products.json, which scrapers/healthplus.py itself reads (line 97). So both sides of every comparison were re-read from the source the scraper already used. This checks drift, not parser correctness.
